campaign.defeat: The Senate will want a report. I will write that the province was well begun and the legate learned quickly. Try again; the coast is still there.
province.end.won: My last count, legate, and then I shall stop counting. Varro sailed for Rome on the Senate’s ship, to account for the province. He took his accounts with him; I have kept a copy. The towns we built stand from the coast to Nova Ostia, and the men who built them are still in the column, older and harder to impress. The province is yours. So, I am told, am I.
province.end.recalled: My last count, legate. Castra has fallen, and with it the Senate’s patience. We sail for Rome on the Senate’s ship, which Varro has kindly lent us, and he stays to govern what we built. I have packed the accounts. They are in order, which will surprise him, and they say what we did here, which will not.
castra.brief:
Legate. The Senate has given you a legion’s worth of tools and a coastline nobody wanted. This is Terra Nova; that hill is your camp.

Rome was not built in a day, but it was built of boards and stone. So: a woodcutter for logs, a sawmill to make boards of them, a stonecutter for the rocks, and a forester, because woodcutters are thorough.

I am Gaius Sestius, your quaestor. I count things. Give me something to count.
castra.debrief: Fifty boards, forty stone. The Senate would call it a start. I call it a camp that will not run out of nails. Next: the men are sleeping under carts.
castra.tip.site: A site. Diggers level it, carriers bring boards and stone, builders raise it. Click it to watch.
castra.tip.tool: He took an axe from the store. Every trade needs its tool. The store has a few of each; a toolsmith makes more, later.
castra.tip.log: A log on the pile. A carrier will fetch it to the sawmill. Nobody needs a road.
castra.tip.board: Boards. Now you can build anything the Senate allows.
castra.tip.panel: Click a building to see what it is doing. Its panel shows the worker, the goods and why it might be waiting.
castra.tip.camera: Getting your bearings? The wheel zooms, right-drag moves the view, Option-drag or Shift + wheel turns it. Esc → Controls has the rest.
castra.tip.speed: Waiting is for senators. The 2× button in the top bar speeds the sun. Nothing else changes.
domus.brief:
Twenty-two carriers marched in with you; sixteen are still with us, and the Senate’s letter is very clear that no more are coming.

A Small Residence brings eight settlers to the camp, a Medium one eighteen. Each new man carries until a building needs him for something better. Build homes.

And a storehouse near the huts: your men carry everything from the headquarters, and every step they save is a board sawn sooner.
domus.debrief: Forty-eight mouths, forty-eight pairs of hands. I have written down both figures; you will want the second. Next: the mouths.
domus.tip.spawn: A settler moved in. He is a carrier until someone needs him. The top bar counts the idle ones.
domus.tip.store: Goods now go to the nearest store. A hut beside it never waits long for its carrier.
domus.tip.badge: A badge over a roof says why it has stopped. Press . to go to the next one. B changes how many you see.
piscis.brief:
Men eat. At present they eat what we brought, which is twenty meals in a pile.

A Fisher’s Hut on the lake shore feeds us from the water; a Hunter’s Hut by the woods lives off the hares, and the woods keep the hares, so keep the woods.

Each hut works within a circle; the ground shows it while you choose the spot. Mines, when we have them, will not turn a wheel without food.
piscis.debrief: Fish and hare. Not Rome’s table, but the men have stopped looking at the mules. Next: bread, which is a longer story.
piscis.tip.fish: A fish. They come back slowly; two fishers on one pond starve each other.
piscis.tip.meat: Meat. Hares live off grown trees. Fell the wood and they leave.
piscis.tip.range: The circle you saw is where he works. Water, game or trees outside it might as well be in Rome.
panem.brief:
Fish and hare feed a camp; bread feeds a province. It takes four buildings, and I will not pretend otherwise.

A Grain Farm sows fields around itself and reaps them in a minute and a half. A Windmill grinds the grain. A Waterworks by the water fills buckets. A Bakery takes flour and water and gives us loaves.

When something stands idle, the Economy tab says what is short. Read it before you build a second of anything.
panem.debrief: Bread. Now the mines can be fed, when there are mines. Next: the border, which is closer than you think.
panem.tip.farm: Grain takes ninety seconds to ripen. The farmer sows first and reaps later; the mill waits meanwhile.
panem.tip.flour: Flour. Flour and water make bread; the bakery’s panel shows both piles.
panem.tip.prio: The starred building comes first. Goods and crews go there before anywhere else. Only one at a time.
panem.tip.economy: The Economy tab. What is made and used each minute, and which tools are short. Read it before building a second of anything.
fines.brief:
Your land ends where the headquarters’ reach ends: a circle, and everything of ours inside it. The mountain to the north-east is outside it, and the mountain is where the iron is.

A Guard Tower claims a smaller circle of its own once a soldier walks into it; a Watchtower a larger one. The headquarters sends the soldier by itself and keeps two back.

Build on land that is not yours and the building burns. Build at the edge and the edge moves. Pioneers, if you have a shovel and a spare man, stake out land with nothing but their feet.
fines.debrief: A tower, and the hill inside it. The Senate likes a border it can see. Next: what the hill is made of.
fines.tip.manned: A soldier walked out of the headquarters by himself. It keeps two back. The border moved with him: look at the minimap.
fines.tip.staked: Staked. Pioneers claim a patch each; a foreign tower takes it back for good.
fines.tip.burn: On land that turns foreign a building burns. Build behind your towers, not beside them.
metalla.brief:
The mountain is inside the border. What is inside the mountain, nobody knows, and I will not have the men digging at random.

Send a geologist. Any free carrier will take the trade; pick the card in the Industry tab and click the mountain. He probes eight spots and leaves a sign at each: black lumps for coal, rust for iron, gold for gold, a cross for nothing.

A mine goes on a sign, or where the rock has begun to glitter. Its marker glows green over a rich vein. And a mine eats: one meal a cart. The larder is full for now.
metalla.debrief: Coal and iron ore, in carts. The smiths will want both, and the miners will want dinner. Next: bars, and tools.
metalla.tip.sign: A sign. What lies beneath and how much. It fades after eight minutes; the ore stays known, and the rock glitters.
metalla.tip.mine: A mine. It eats one meal a cart: bread, fish or meat. Watch its food pile.
metalla.tip.geologist: He set out with a hammer. Geologists work only inside your border, and need a store on this land to come home to.
ferrum.brief:
Ore is a rock with ambitions. An Iron Smelter turns it into bars with coal; a Toolsmith turns bars into tools with more coal. Two coal mines for one smelter is the rule of thumb.

You will have noticed the second sawmill standing idle. It wants a saw, and the store had one. The toolsmith forges whatever idle buildings lack; the sliders in the Economy tab tell him what to stockpile.

Iron feeds tools, weapons, warships and engines. Everything from here on begins at that furnace.
ferrum.debrief: Every man has his tool again. I have stopped hearing about it. Next: arms.
ferrum.tip.iron: A bar of iron. Tools, weapons, warships and engines all begin here.
ferrum.tip.tool: A tool. The toolsmith forges what idle buildings lack; a slider in the Economy tab makes him stockpile one.
ferrum.tip.saw: The second sawmill wants a saw. The store had one. Until the toolsmith forges another, it stands.
arma.brief:
Seven soldiers hold this province, and two of them are the headquarters’ own. The Senate does not call that a garrison; it calls it a rumour.

A Weaponsmith beats bars into swords and bows; the slider on its panel says which. Barracks take one weapon and one idle carrier and give back a soldier, and they leave four carriers free however many weapons wait, so homes come before recruits.

Gold, if the mountain has any, does nothing but sit in the store; it happens to make every soldier fight harder while it does.
arma.debrief: Twelve soldiers. The Ninth had four thousand, and look where that got them. Next: the road, and who is on it.
arma.tip.recruit: A recruit. One weapon and one idle carrier. He walks to the headquarters and waits for a tower to need him.
arma.tip.weapon: A weapon. Swordsmen hold a line; bowmen shoot over it. The weaponsmith’s slider sets the mix.
arma.tip.gold: Gold. In the store it raises morale: up to sixty percent harder blows at twenty-five bars.
arma.tip.idle: The barracks keep four carriers free. Build homes for more men, or they train nobody.
pugna.brief:
Deserters of the Ninth Legion hold two towers on the road east and call themselves free men. The Senate calls them something shorter.

Select a tower of theirs and press Attack, and your men march by themselves. Or command them: drag a box around your soldiers, right-click where they should go or what they should storm, and a number key with Ctrl keeps a group under it. A captured tower keeps its land and its walls.

They will not take it kindly. When they come, select a tower of yours, call out its garrison to meet them, and R sends the men back to their posts.
pugna.debrief: The road is ours. The deserters were not many, and are fewer. Next: the gods, who have been patient.
pugna.tip.march: They march. Swordsmen in front, bowmen behind. The tower’s garrison comes out to meet them.
pugna.tip.taken: Captured. A taken tower keeps its land. One man of yours mans it now; it wants more.
pugna.tip.raid: The deserters come for their tower. Select a tower of yours and Call out its garrison to meet them. R sends the men back.
pugna.tip.group: Groups. Box-select soldiers, then Ctrl (or Option) and a number key keeps them under it. The number picks them again; twice takes you there.
pugna.raid: They are coming for it. Call out the garrison, legate; a tower is worth a fight.
dei.brief:
The priests have written to the Senate, and the Senate has written to me. A province without a temple is a camp, they say, whatever its walls.

A Vineyard grows the wine; carriers take it to a Temple, where the priest offers it and the gods answer in mana. The Faith tab holds what you can ask of them.

Blessed Harvest ripens every field and vine in its circle at once. Healing Light mends your soldiers and puts iron in their arms for a minute. Both reach only so far from your strongholds. Ask for both; I want to see the priests earn their keep.
dei.debrief: The priests are content and the fields are early. I distrust both, but I will take the grain. Next: donkeys.
dei.tip.wine: Wine. Carriers take it to the temple; the priest offers it. Nobody drinks it, which I find hard to believe.
dei.tip.offering: An offering. Three mana a cycle, up to a hundred and fifty. Spells need a temple, a priest at his post and reach from a stronghold.
dei.tip.cast: The gods answered. Four seconds, and the priests can ask again.
mercatura.brief:
The far side of the mountain has the better veins, so the mines are there, with a storehouse and a watchtower, and the food is here. The miners are eating the walk.

A Market Place is the end of a road. Build one here and one there; in one, choose the other as destination and click + on the goods to send, and carriers stock them. A Donkey Ranch breeds the donkeys that carry them, two goods a trip, fed on grain and water.

Twelve goods delivered up the road, and the miners will stop writing to me.
mercatura.debrief: The mines are fed and the donkeys are not consulted. That is trade. Next: the sea.
mercatura.tip.market: A market. The end of a road. Its panel: choose the other market, then + on the goods to send.
mercatura.tip.donkey: A donkey. It waits at a market with goods to carry; two a trip.
mercatura.tip.caravan: Delivered. Carriers at the far end take it on to whoever needs it.
mare.brief:
There is an island off this coast, and the fishermen say it glitters. The Senate has heard the fishermen.

A Harbour goes on the shore beside deep water; a Shipyard likewise, and it builds a ship from ten boards. A harbour can send an expedition: a builder, a digger, a soldier, two carriers and the makings of a second harbour, by ship, to found a colony where you point.

Once the colony stands and a soldier mans it, ships carry goods between your harbours by themselves, or as you order.
mare.debrief: A harbour, a ship, a colony. Rome began smaller, though it did not have to swim. Next: engines.
mare.tip.launch: A ship. Twenty goods or twelve settlers. It waits at your harbour for orders.
mare.tip.expedition: An expedition gathers. Five people and a harbour’s worth of boards and stone at the dock; the ship takes them over.
mare.tip.landed: Landed. The colony’s harbour holds the shore until its soldier mans it.
mare.tip.unloaded: Unloaded. Ships keep a colony supplied by themselves; Shipping orders send what you choose.
machinae.brief:
The Ninth again: a watchtower and two guard towers on the hill road, and this time they have bowmen on the walls. Men at the door of a manned watchtower die at the door.

A Siege Workshop builds catapults from boards and iron. Select one and right-click a stronghold: its stones kill the garrison first, then bring the walls down. It cannot fight, so send swordsmen with it, formed up in front, and tell them to stand firm.

Their tower is out of the catapult’s range from your land, so it must roll out beyond the border. Escort it.
machinae.debrief: The tower fell without a man of ours at its door. Engineers are worth their iron. Next: the fleet.
machinae.tip.machine: A catapult. Select it and right-click a stronghold. It cannot fight back: send swordsmen along.
machinae.tip.hit: A stone through the roof. One of the garrison falls with each hit; an empty tower loses its walls.
machinae.tip.razed: Walls down. A ruined tower gives its land back.
machinae.tip.firm: Stand firm. Select the escort and set a formation and Stand firm in their panel: they hold their line instead of chasing.
classis.brief:
The Ninth have taken to the water: a tower on the shore north of the harbour and a ship that stops ours. Land is my business; this is yours.

The shipyard’s panel has a switch: Warship. Twelve boards and three iron fittings, and a catapult on the foredeck. Select the warship and right-click an enemy ship to hunt it, or a stronghold by the water to shell it; it stands off beyond the archers’ reach where the coast allows.

A battered ship mends at its harbour. Bring it home between fights.
classis.debrief: A warship of our own. Varro will have heard the news by now. Next: Varro.
classis.tip.warship: A warship. Right-click a ship to hunt it, a shore tower to shell it. It keeps beyond the archers where it can.
classis.tip.broadside: A stone from the foredeck. Twenty of a ship’s hundred and twenty; a tower’s garrison falls a man a hit.
classis.tip.sinking: She goes down. Everyone aboard is lost with a ship. Mend yours at a harbour between fights.
provincia.brief:
Quintus Varro, legate of Nova Ostia, has declared his colony independent of the Senate, and therefore of us. He has a headquarters, towers, a harbour and ambitions.

You have everything this province has taught you, and the Senate has opened its last doors: the Castle, and the Great Temple with the Wrath of the Heavens in it.

Take or raze his strongholds one after another until the last lays down its arms. A colony whose headquarters falls cannot hide its towers, and one down to its last three will yield. The sea gives you ten minutes’ truce. Use them.
provincia.debrief: The last of Varro’s towers strikes its colours. Terra Nova is a province of Rome, and you are its governor. I have counted everything. It comes to: enough. The maps beyond are yours to draw: Free play, any size, any rivals.
provincia.tip.truce: The truce is over. Varro may march at any time. Towers on the road towards him, manned.
provincia.tip.fallen: His headquarters is down. His towers show through the fog now. Three left and no castle: he yields.
provincia.tip.castle: A castle. Ten men and the widest circle a stronghold claims. A realm with a castle never yields.
provincia.truceover: The truce is over. Varro may march at any time. I would have towers on the road by now.
saltus.brief:
The Senate’s governor has landed at Nova Ostia, and his first act was to close the pass. The road east runs through Saltus; so, now, do his toll, his fort and, I am told, his priests.

The valley is ours and nothing in it is built. Wood, stone, homes, bread: you know the order. The mountain in the south-west has coal and iron, and we will want both before the snow.

He will not come himself. He will send men through the pass, a few at first and more each time. Put a tower at our end of it and keep men in it. When we are ready, we go through the other way.
saltus.debrief: The fort at the far end flies our colours and the road east is open. Varro has written to the Senate that we attacked him. I have written that we were in a hurry. Next: the province, one region at a time.
saltus.tip.raid: Men in the pass. They go for the tower nearest them. Its garrison fights at the door; the headquarters sends more.
saltus.tip.wall: The dark ridge is sheer rock. Nobody walks over it or builds on it. The pass is the way east, and the goat path, if you find it.
saltus.tip.frozen: Frost. Varro’s priests. The frozen can still be struck; send the next men in behind, not with them.
saltus.letter: A letter from Nova Ostia. To the camp in the valley. The pass is closed by order of the Senate. Those who would use it will pay the toll at the fort, or turn back. — Q. Varro, governor.
saltus.goat: A way over the wall. In the north the rock is low enough for goats, and for men who do not mind goats. It comes down behind his fort.
saltus.toll: Another letter. Your men fight well for men without a governor. The toll has doubled.
saltus.counter: The fort is the Senate’s. I shall have it back before the week is out, and the men who took it.
saltus.held: They broke on the walls. Varro has lost his fort twice in a week. He will write to the Senate about it, at length.
silva.brief:
Varro has sold the forest. Not to anyone we know: to a timber company of Nova Ostia, which is to say to Varro, who owns it. His loggers are working in from the north-east and they are not slow.

In the middle of the wood there is an old grove, open ground round a spring, that nobody has built on because the men say it is haunted. Take it. Ground that is flat, watered and haunted is worth three that are only flat.

And somewhere in the north-west are the Ninth, what is left of them after Prima Pugna: forty deserters in a camp, cold and hungry. Hungry men can be fought. They can also be fed.
silva.debrief: The forest is ours, the loggers are gone, and the Ninth eat at our table. I have entered them in the rolls as reinforcements. The Senate need not know where from. Next: the province, one region at a time.
silva.tip.wood: The wood is thick. Every tree is a board, and in the way of every building. Woodcutters by the sites you want.
silva.tip.raid: The company’s guards. They come for the tower nearest their stockade.
silva.tip.turncoat: Turned. The Ninth’s towers fly our colours now, their men in them.
silva.lease: A notice from Nova Ostia. The Senate has leased the forest of Silva to the timber company of Nova Ostia. Anyone found felling in it will be treated as a thief, and anyone found living in it as a squatter. — Q. Varro, governor.
silva.grove: The old grove. The men say it is haunted. I say it is flat, it has water, and nobody has built on it yet.
silva.ninth: The Ninth. Cold, hungry and ashamed of it. Twenty loaves in a store of ours near their camp and they might remember whose soldiers they were.
silva.fed: The Ninth have eaten our bread. And taken our side. Their centurion says he would like a word with Varro, when it is convenient, and a sword when it is not.
silva.stockade: On the matter of the timber. Men who steal the Senate’s timber are hanged at Nova Ostia. I mention it only for your records.
vallis.brief:
The best farmland in the province lies in a valley between two walls of mountains, a day’s march long. Varro has granted it to a colony of his veterans, who arrived at the east end this morning with ploughs and surveyors.

We arrived at the west end this morning with ploughs and no surveyors. The Senate’s rule is old and simple: land belongs to whoever holds it. So hold it: towers claim ground, and his colonists are building fast.

They will not fight while the harvest stands in the fields. After the harvest, I would not count on it.
vallis.debrief: The valley is ours to the lake and beyond it, and the granaries are full. Varro’s veterans have gone back to Nova Ostia to be veterans somewhere else. Next: the province, one region at a time.
vallis.tip.race: A race, for now. His colonists will not attack before the harvest. Their towers claim land as fast as ours: build where the valley is still nobody’s.
vallis.tip.captured: Taken. A captured tower keeps its land. The more of his you hold, the less valley is his.
vallis.deed: A deed of grant. The valley is granted to the veterans’ colony of Nova Ostia. Your settlers may stay where they stand. Where they stand is not to move.
vallis.third: The valley is filling up. A sixth of it flies our flag. Varro’s surveyors are measuring the rest very quickly.
vallis.harvest: The harvest is in. And the survey is finished. What is not mine by the survey will be mine by other means.
aurum.brief:
The gold of Terra Nova is on top of a table of rock with cliffs all round it, and there is one path up. Varro’s mining company holds the top of it, with a watchtower where the path comes over the rim.

Take the foot of the path, then the tower, and the mines are ours to work. Miners eat. Every loaf will go up that path on a carrier’s back.

The hill tribes in the north-west have been watching the path for longer than Varro has owned it. They will watch us too.
aurum.debrief: The gold comes down the path in carts now, and the bread goes up. The tribes have learned to wave at the carters, which is more than they ever did for Varro. Next: the province, one region at a time.
aurum.tip.cliff: The dark rim is sheer. Nobody climbs it. The path is the only way up, for us and for the carts.
aurum.tip.raid: Tribesmen on the path. They go for the tower at the top. Keep it full.
aurum.claim: On the matter of the plateau. The gold of Metalla is the Senate’s, and the Senate has let it to my company. Trespass on the path is theft, whatever the tribes may have told you.
aurum.path: The path is ours. Every loaf for the miners goes up it now, and the tribes know it as well as we do. Keep men at the tower.
aurum.tribes: The tribes. Not Varro’s men: the hills’ own. They take what comes up the path, and they have always taken it.
aurum.friends: The tribes are watching the path. For us, this time. Word has come down from Collis: the carts go up the path unmolested, and anyone else’s do not.
collis.brief:
The upland belongs to the tribes, who have never paid the Senate a tax or Varro a toll, and hold three hills to prove it: a fort on each, one way up each, and their chief behind them in the north.

Hill forts are taken the hard way, one path at a time. Or the other way: the tribes feast before they talk. A store of ours below a hill with fifteen loaves and ten joints of meat in it, and that hill may decide it was always our friend.

Take two, by either means, and I wager the third sends its chief down to talk.
collis.debrief: The upland is ours by right of two hills taken and one that came to dinner. The tribes will fight beside us now. They have asked, very politely, to be pointed at Varro. Next: the province, one region at a time.
collis.tip.turncoat: A hill has come over. Its men fight for us now, and its land is ours.
collis.tip.raid: The chief’s men. Out of the north, for the nearest tower of ours.
collis.feast0: A feast. The hill ate our bread and our meat, and its men came down singing. They are ours now, and they sing worse sober.
collis.feast1: A feast. The hill ate our bread and our meat, and its men came down singing. They are ours now, and they sing worse sober.
collis.feast2: A feast. The hill ate our bread and our meat, and its men came down singing. They are ours now, and they sing worse sober.
collis.yield: The third hill has sent its chief. With a goat and a speech. We accepted the goat.
ara.brief:
On the hill in the middle of Ara stands the Great Temple of the province, older than Rome’s claim to it, and Varro’s priests are in it. They can call down lightning, freeze a cohort where it stands, and turn a soldier’s loyalty in his hands. They have been practising.

Three towers keep the hilltop; two paths go up, the pilgrims’ from our side and the priests’ from his. Take the towers and the hill, and the temple with it: a temple goes to whoever holds its ground.

But take it standing. If it burns, the Senate will hear that the legate burned the gods’ house, and the gods will hear it first.
ara.debrief: The temple is ours and its priests have changed their prayers. They tell me the gods did not notice. I have entered the temple in the accounts as “restored”. Next: the province, one region at a time.
ara.tip.frozen: Frost. The frozen can still be struck. Send the next men in behind, not beside them.
ara.tip.turncoat: The temple has changed hands. With the ground it stands on. Its priests serve us now, if we bring them wine.
ara.hymn: From the governor, at Ara. The gods of this province have always been on the Senate’s side. I should not like you to find out how.
ara.convert: Converted. Three of ours walked over to his side with a hymn on their lips. Do not stand them in a crowd under his hill.
ara.restored: The temple is ours. Standing, and with its priests in it, who have changed their prayers. They say the gods did not notice.
aestuarium.brief:
The estuary runs up from the sea right through the land, a day’s sail, and cuts the province in two: our bank on the west, the east bank on the other side of the water, rich, empty and out of reach of anything that walks. Gold on the hill across from the bay, and more in the north-east.

A harbour in the bay at the head, a shipyard, a ship; then a colony on the far bank, and the ships keep it supplied. What the colony digs, the ships bring back. Every cargo is a round trip across the water.

Varro has farmed the estuary’s dues to the pirates on the islet off its mouth. They will not come for our harbours. They will come for our ships, as soon as they see a cargo land, and they will keep coming.
aestuarium.debrief: The estuary is ours from the head to the mouth. The pirates’ flotillas are on the bottom of it, which the fishermen say is good for the fish. Next: the province, one region at a time.
aestuarium.tip.expedition: An expedition gathers. Five people and a harbour’s worth of boards and stone at the dock; the ship takes them across.
aestuarium.tip.unloaded: A cargo landed. The pirates saw it too.
aestuarium.tip.fleet: Pirates. They go for our ships, not our walls. A ship moored under a tower is safer than one crossing; a warship beside it, safer still.
aestuarium.tip.sinking: She goes down. Everyone and everything aboard with her. A battered warship mends at its harbour.
aestuarium.dues: On the dues of the estuary. The dues of the estuary are farmed to a company of honest seamen. They keep seamen’s hours and seamen’s accounts, and I cannot answer for either. — Q. Varro, governor.
aestuarium.sails: A hull in the water. The pirates at the mouth will have seen it. When they see a cargo land, they come up the estuary. A warship at the harbour and a tower by the dock would give them something to think about.
aestuarium.flotilla1: A sail at the mouth. One ship, low in the water and fast. It will go for whatever of ours is afloat, then back to the islet to wait for the next.
aestuarium.flotilla2: A letter from Nova Ostia. I am told the collectors of the estuary have lost a ship. I have written to them to be more careful.
aestuarium.flotilla3: The whole flotilla. Three of them, the Lupa in front: everything the islet has left. If these go down, the estuary is ours.
aestuarium.peace: No sails at the mouth. Since Litus the pirates keep to their islet, and send their compliments. Our ships may cross as they please.
aestuarium.clear: The estuary is clear. Three flotillas on the bottom. The dues of the estuary will be collected by us from now on, and honestly, which will be a novelty for it.
insulae.brief:
West of the estuary the coast breaks up into islands, a dozen if you count the rocks, four worth a harbour. Varro keeps his fleet at a base on the biggest of them, in the north-east, and calls the rest the Senate’s.

The Senate has never seen them. Put a colony on three and they are the province’s, which is to say ours. His colonists will be putting ashore too, sooner or later; the islands go to whoever lands first.

The pirates have a tower on two of them, on the gold and on the iron, and his warships will shell any harbour of ours they find. Neither can be reached on foot. Both can be reached with a catapult on a deck.
insulae.debrief: Three islands fly our colours and the pirates’ towers are rubble in the surf. Varro writes that his fleet was “dispersed by weather”. I have checked: it was fine all week. Next: the province, one region at a time.
insulae.tip.expedition: An expedition gathers. Five people and a harbour’s worth of boards and stone at the dock; the ship takes them over.
insulae.tip.landed: Landed. The colony’s harbour holds the shore until its soldier mans it. Ships keep it supplied by themselves.
insulae.tip.fleet: Varro’s warships. They shell the nearest harbour or tower of ours they can reach. Meet them at sea.
insulae.tip.sinking: She goes down. Everyone aboard is lost with her. Mend yours at a harbour between fights.
insulae.licence: On the islands of the province. The islands of Terra Nova are the Senate’s, and the Senate’s fleet keeps them. Settlers found on them without my licence will be treated as pirates, and so, for that matter, will the pirates. — Q. Varro, governor.
insulae.rival: Varro’s colonists. His ships have put settlers ashore on one of the islands. A harbour of his is a stronghold like any other: it can be shelled, and the island settled after.
insulae.landed: Our first island. The flag is up and the harbour is building. Varro will have it reported by the evening and shelled by the morning, if we give him the morning.
insulae.squadron: An unlicensed settlement. An unlicensed settlement has been reported on the Senate’s islands. The fleet will attend to it.
insulae.aquila: To the legate. Two islands. You are either very brave or very badly advised. The Aquila will explain the difference.
insulae.towers: A pirate tower down. Shelled from a ship, which the pirates think very unsporting, having done it to everyone else for years.
litus.brief:
The pirates Varro hired live on an island off this coast, in a harbour with towers either side of it and a flagship in front: the Corvus, which we sank once at Classis, or thought we did. This one is twice the size and flies the same rag.

They cannot land and neither can we. So this is a fleet war: a harbour and a shipyard, iron for the fittings, and warships, as many as the yard can launch. They will come across to shell our coast and sink our ships while we build.

Sink the Corvus and burn the harbour she hides in. Pirates without a harbour are fishermen with bad manners.
litus.debrief: The Corvus is on the bottom, and this time I watched her go. The pirates’ harbour is ash. Their survivors have asked to join our fleet; I have said we will think about it, which they understand to mean yes. Next: the province, one region at a time.
litus.tip.warship: A warship. Right-click a ship to hunt it, a stronghold by the water to shell it. Several together finish a fight before it finishes them.
litus.tip.fleet: Raiders. Across from the island for our ships and our coast. A warship at the harbour meets them; the harbour mends it after.
litus.tip.sinking: She goes down. Everyone aboard is lost with her.
litus.letter: On the pirates of the south coast. I am told there are pirates on the south coast. I have never met them. I have, I confess, paid them, but for one season only, and I cannot be blamed if they have taken a liking to the work.
litus.corvus: The Corvus. Three hundred and sixty of a warship’s hundred and twenty, by the look of her timbers. Do not send one ship. Send four, and bring them home to mend.
litus.raid1: Sails from the island. A raider, come across to see what we have afloat and what we have built by the water. More will follow while their harbour stands.
litus.sunk: The Corvus is on the bottom. Where she belongs, and this time I have seen it with my own eyes. So have the pirates.
litus.burnt: Their harbour burns. No more raiders will come from it. What ships they have left have nowhere to mend.
castellum.brief:
Between the valley and Nova Ostia stands Castellum: a hill with cliffs round it and Varro’s hall on top, and four castles round its foot, one at each way up and one on each flank. Every road to his capital goes past them.

Castles do not yield and cannot be rushed. Ten men in each, archers on the walls, and they come out to meet whatever comes near. Catapults take them from beyond the archers’ reach: a siege workshop, iron for the engines, and swordsmen to stand in front of them.

His priests are on the hill. They will freeze a storming party at the gate and call lightning on a crowd. Spread out, and bring a temple of our own.
castellum.debrief: Castellum has fallen: four castles and the hall on the hill. Varro has written to the Senate that it was never meant to be held. I have written that it was held, for a while, by him. Next: Nova Ostia, when the province is ready.
castellum.tip.machine: A catapult. Select it and right-click a castle. It cannot fight: swordsmen in front of it, told to stand firm.
castellum.tip.frozen: Frost. His priests. The frozen can still be struck; the next men in behind, not beside them.
castellum.tip.razed: Walls down. A castle that falls gives its land back, and the next one is closer.
castellum.letter: From the hall at Castellum. Castellum has never been taken. It was built by men who expected you, and it is held by men who have been told about you.
castellum.wrath: Lightning. His priests saw a crowd and asked the sky about it. Fewer men at a time, and from more sides.
castellum.sortie1: A sortie. The castles are sending men out against our nearest tower. They will go back in if they can; do not let them.
castellum.breach: On the matter of one castle. You have one castle. I have three, and the hill, and the Senate. My garrison has been told to stop waiting for you.
castellum.hall: The hall on the hill is burning. Varro was not in it. He left for Nova Ostia a day ago, which I take to mean he knew before we did.
novaostia.brief:
Nova Ostia: Varro’s capital on the east coast, behind a wall of mountains with two passes through it and a castle at the far end of each, his fleet in the bay, and his two client colonies on our flanks, north and south, who hold their charters from him.

Everything we have comes with us: the column, the wagons, every region’s gift. He has the Senate’s money, a sharp garrison and ten minutes of truce while his heralds ride; after that he marches, and he does not stop.

And the Senate has sent a ship with its verdict on the two of us. Whoever holds Nova Ostia when it docks is the governor it will find. Take his headquarters before it does.
novaostia.debrief: Nova Ostia has opened its gates. The Senate’s ship came in on the same tide, and the verdict it carried named the governor of Terra Nova. The name has been changed. The ink is still wet. The province is yours.
novaostia.tip.truce: The truce is over. His legions march now, and his colonies with them. The towers on our flanks first.
novaostia.tip.machine: A catapult. For the castles at the passes: from beyond their archers, swordsmen in front.
novaostia.tip.fleet: His squadrons. Out of the bay for our coast. Warships meet them; the harbour mends.
novaostia.letter: From the governor’s seat. You have come a long way to be recalled. The Senate’s ship is on the sea; I have asked it to take you home.
novaostia.truce: The heralds are back. My colonies have their orders, and so have my legions. Let us see which of us the Senate finds standing.
novaostia.sighted: A sail on the horizon. The Senate’s, low and slow and heavy with seals. Half an hour to Nova Ostia, by the look of the wind.
novaostia.close: Ten minutes. The Senate’s ship has rounded the point. If his hall is standing when it ties up, the verdict is his to read.
novaostia.colony0: A charter withdrawn. The northern colony has lost its charter, and its colonists their homes. I shall find the Senate other colonists.
novaostia.colony1: A charter withdrawn. The southern colony too. You are very thorough, legate. So is the Senate.
novaostia.gates: The gates are open. His hall is burning and his seal is in my hand. Whatever towers he still holds, Nova Ostia is ours when the Senate’s ship ties up.
defence.castra.brief:
Varro has come for Castra itself: the camp we raised plank by plank, the town it became, and the men who built it. If it falls, the Senate recalls the legate, and I go with him.

Four waves, the scouts say, each heavier than the last. The towers towards him are manned; the barracks can make more. Keep the headquarters standing.
defence.castra.debrief: Castra held. The Senate will hear that the governor came to the capital and went home without it. Back to the province.
defence.castra.tip.wave: A wave. They come for the tower nearest their camp. Select it and Call out its garrison, or send men from the headquarters to stand beside it.
defence.castra.march: A word before the fighting. You may still surrender the capital with honour. After today you will not have the choice, or the capital.
defence.castra.last: The last of them. His veterans, at the back where veterans stand. When these break, it is over.
defence.silva.brief:
Varro’s legion is on the road to Silva. The scouts count them in hundreds, which means in dozens, but good dozens.

The town stands as we left it. Fill the towers on his side, keep the barracks busy, and do not let them reach the headquarters. If it falls, the region is his again.
defence.silva.debrief: Silva held. His legion went home lighter than it came, and fewer. Back to the province.
defence.silva.tip.wave: A wave. They come for the tower nearest their camp. Select it and Call out its garrison, or send men from the headquarters to stand beside it.
defence.silva.march: A word before the fighting. Give me Silva and your men may keep their swords. Make me take it and they will not.
defence.silva.last: The last of them. His veterans, at the back where veterans stand. When these break, it is over.

defence.aestuarium.brief:
Varro’s fleet has put out for Aestuarium. Nobody can march on it, so he will not try: four squadrons, the lookouts say, to shell the harbour and the towers by the water until there is nothing left to hold the coast.

The town stands as we left it, with a warship at the dock and iron in store for more. Meet them at sea; a battered ship mends at the harbour. If the headquarters falls, the region is his again.

dispatch.appointed: The Senate has appointed me governor of Terra Nova. You will hand over the coast, the camp and the men at Castra, and return to Rome to account for them.
dispatch.held.castra: Castra held. His legion went home lighter than it came.
dispatch.strike.castra: The Senate’s patience is at an end, and so is mine. I am coming to Castra for the men who built it.
dispatch.won.silva: Silva is ours. 40 boards and 20 logs to every start; the Ninth’s veterans.
dispatch.lost.silva: Silva is lost. We will have to take it again, and he will have fortified it.
dispatch.held.silva: Silva held. His legion went home lighter than it came.
dispatch.strike.silva: Silva was never yours to hold. My legion is on the road to it.
dispatch.fortify.silva: Varro has fortified Silva: more men in its towers, and more of them on the roads out of it. It will cost more to take.
dispatch.won.saltus: Saltus is ours. 12 iron and 12 coal to every start: the pass’s mines.
dispatch.lost.saltus: Saltus is lost. We will have to take it again, and he will have fortified it.
